question: Contrastive learning is an effective technique for learning good discriminative embedding representations, and was a popular training strategy for encoder-only LMs. With the recent popularity of causal, decoder-only LMs, have there been any works which show that contrastive learning can also help improve generative performance for this architecture?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer directly affirms that contrastive learning has been applied to causal, decoder-only LMs to improve generative performance, not just discriminative embeddings.
examples: Yes, works such as CoNT show contrastive learning can help generative models
Contrastive learning is not limited to representation learning; it improves text generation quality

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies CoNT (Contrastive Neural Text Generation) by name as the concrete work demonstrating contrastive learning benefits for text generation.
examples: CoNT proposes a new contrastive neural text generation framework
One example is Contrastive Neural Text Generation (CoNT)

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that contrastive learning alleviates exposure bias, where autoregressive models trained only on ground-truth sequences generalize poorly at inference.
examples: Training only on ground truths causes poor generalization; contrastive examples address this
Contrastive learning offers a new solution to exposure bias

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that CoNT samples contrastive examples from the model's own predictions (e.g., beam search), exposing it to inference-stage mistakes, unlike naive contrastive learning.
examples: CoNT draws negatives from its own beam-search outputs
This differs from naive CL, which does not use self-generated samples

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes CoNT's N-pairs contrastive loss, which treats contrastive examples fine-grainedly according to sequence-level scores (e.g., BLEU), enabling the model to learn a better sequence-level distance function between source and target representations.
examples: An N-pairs loss weights examples based on their sequence-level BLEU scores
The loss learns a sequence-level distance between source and target representations using ground truth and self-generated examples

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer mentions that contrastive learning provides a sequence-level loss complementing the conventional token-level MLE loss, aligning with sequence-level evaluation metrics used in MT and summarization.
examples: A sequence-level loss supplements token-level MLE
Tasks like MT and summarization are evaluated on sequence-level metrics such as BLEU

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that CoNT incorporates the learned sequence similarity score into decoding, helping find better global configurations than pure LM-likelihood decoding.
examples: The learned sequence-level distance is used at decoding time
This helps find a better global configuration than likelihood-only decoding

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer discusses DExperts as a related contrastive-style approach that ensembles expert and anti-expert LMs at decoding time for controlled generation, and clarifies that, unlike CoNT, it does not use contrastive signals during training.
examples: DExperts combines expert and anti-expert LMs in a product of experts at decoding time
Two paradigms: CoNT's contrastive training vs. DExperts' contrastive decoding-time steering
